prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Transparent production brush-stamp atlas for a Chinese overhead ink-wash terrain map with edge-matching hexagonal tiles. Square, strict 4 by 4 grid of 16 separate sprites, each fully isolated with generous alpha margins. Orthographic straight-down view. First row: four variations of a long narrow horizontal mountain RIDGE STRIP viewed from directly above, an undulating pale crest running continuously from left to right with dense charcoal grey-green cun hachures along both flanks, feathered brush tips, ratio approximately 3 to 1, ends fade gently. Second row: an overhead curved ridge elbow; a Y-shaped overhead ridge junction; a three-way overhead saddle; a small overhead rugged ridge knot. Third row: a tiny traditional Chinese junk boat seen vertically from above, long hull and pale folded sail; another overhead small wooden fishing boat; an overhead coastal hamlet of six tiny grey tile rooftops and a short pier; a second overhead harbor hamlet with three rooftops and a jetty. Fourth row: an overhead scattered coastal boulder cluster; an overhead sandy shoal; an overhead tiny irregular island with grey-green foliage and soft pale shore; a sparse overhead grove of small tree canopies. Authentic hand-painted Chinese water-ink and mineral pigment textures, desaturated malachite grey-green, charcoal and ivory, very restrained tiny cinnabar accents on boats. No perspective skyline, no front-facing mountain triangles, no horizon, no isometric view, no directional shadows. These sprites are atoms for assembling a continuous map, not individual complete tile pictures. No hexagons, no cell backgrounds, no paper, no text, no labels, no grid marks, no watermark. REAL transparent alpha around every brush edge.
